title: Standardize Private metric names/labels, cap cardinality, and define migrations
creator: Logan Wright
description:
Private installs need a bounded, consistent metric surface that is safe for customer-managed Prometheus (especially on-prem) and stable across upgrades.

This ticket standardizes:
- Metric naming (prefixes, units, suffixes, histogram conventions)
- Label keys and allowed values (to avoid unbounded cardinality)
- Cross-service consistency (same label keys mean the same thing)
- Backwards-compatibility plan for any renamed/removed metrics (including recording rules and dashboards)

Primary problems observed in early Private staging and customer escalations:
- High-cardinality labels (route/model/tenant/request_id) causing TSDB churn and slow Grafana queries
- Inconsistent label sets across gateway/router/runtime making dashboards brittle
- Metric renames between builds without migration notes, leading to blank panels after upgrades

Scope (v1): control plane services, API gateway, routing/policy engine, serving runtime pods, and installer/upgrade controller metrics exported to Prometheus.

Non-goals: defining customer-specific dimensions (e.g., per-tenant metrics) as first-class labels in the minimum pack; those should be addressed via logs/traces or optional, explicitly gated metrics.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Publish an agreed metric naming + label contract for Private (doc link in ticket), aligned with observability standards.
2) Identify and fix the top sources of unbounded cardinality in Private-exported metrics (route/model/tenant/request_id/user_id equivalents).
3) Ensure the minimum-pack dashboards and alert rules work against the standardized metrics in a reference Private install.
4) Provide an upgrade/rollback-safe migration plan:
   - Old metric names available for >= 2 releases OR via compatibility recording rules
   - Clear deprecation notes and a removal timeline
   - One-page 'what changed' for Support/PS
5) Add basic automated guardrails: a CI check or smoke test assertion that rejects newly introduced unbounded labels (or at least flags them).
implementation_notes:
Proposed conventions (Private):

Naming:
- Service-level metrics: redwood_<service>_<thing>_<unit>
  Examples:
  - redwood_gateway_http_requests_total
  - redwood_router_request_latency_seconds (histogram)
  - redwood_runtime_tokens_generated_total
- Latency: *_duration_seconds or *_latency_seconds (histogram preferred)
- Resource: use Prometheus/kubelet/cAdvisor metrics where possible; Redwood-specific should not duplicate node exporter/cAdvisor.

Histograms:
- Use Prometheus histogram with _bucket/_sum/_count.
- Buckets should be tuned to LLM inference latencies (ms to tens of seconds). Avoid per-route buckets.

Labels (allowed set, bounded):
- Required common labels where applicable:
  - service: gateway|router|runtime|controlplane-<name>
  - cluster: logical cluster id (installer-provided, low cardinality)
  - namespace
  - pod (only on low-volume 'debug' metrics; avoid on high QPS counters)
  - route: allowed only if it is one of a bounded, configured set (see below)
  - model: allowed only if it is one of a bounded, configured set (see below)
  - status_code / result: use coarse result labels (success|error|timeout|canceled) over raw error strings
- Explicitly forbidden/unbounded labels in the minimum pack:
  - request_id / trace_id
  - raw tenant_id / user_id / api_key_id
  - prompt_hash / input_length_exact (use bucketing)
  - error_message, exception, stacktrace

Cardinality controls:
- Introduce allowlists and 'overflow' buckets:
  - route is normalized to a bounded name (e.g., 'chat.completions', 'embeddings') not the full HTTP path.
  - model label set is capped to top N active models (default N=10), rest => model='other'.
  - tenant dimension is removed from Prometheus by default; if required for some customers, expose via an opt-in feature flag that uses hashed tenant buckets with an explicit maximum bucket count.
- Any opt-in high-cardinality dimensions must be gated behind a Helm value and clearly marked 'unsupported for minimum pack'.

Cross-service alignment:
- Router and runtime should share the same route/model label semantics to keep dashboards stable.
- Gateway uses route label only after normalization (no raw paths).

Guardrails:
- Add a small unit test / metrics lint step to validate:
  - label keys are from an allowlist
  - any label with potentially unbounded values is absent in the default build
  - histograms use seconds
- Add a 'cardinality budget' note in the doc for Support guidance (what to ask customers to disable first if Prometheus is struggling).
migration_plan:
Compatibility strategy (Private):

- For any renamed metric, keep the old metric exported for 2 releases where feasible.
- If we cannot keep old names (e.g., due to library changes), ship recording rules in the observability pack that recreate the old series names from the new metric, with a prominent deprecation note.

Documentation:
- Add an 'Upgrading from <= runtime-1.17' section:
  - list of renamed metrics
  - dashboards/alerts that were updated
  - how to validate post-upgrade (queries to run)

Support readiness:
- Provide a short runbook snippet: 'Dashboards blank after upgrade' with the top 3 likely causes:
  (1) datasource mismatch, (2) metric rename without rules applied, (3) scrape failures due to NetworkPolicy.

Rollback:
- Ensure that upgrading does not delete old metrics immediately (avoid breaking rollback to previous dashboards/alerts).
risks:
Risk: removing labels that customers rely on for internal chargeback.
Mitigation: keep such dimensions in logs and document export patterns; make any Prometheus per-tenant metrics explicitly opt-in and not part of 'supported minimum'.

Risk: dashboards/alerts become too coarse without route/model labels.
Mitigation: keep bounded route/model labels, but ensure overflow buckets ('other') and provide a 'topk' panel built off recording rules.

Risk: label allowlists drift across services.
Mitigation: centralize label contract in a shared module / constants and add CI linting.

Risk: compatibility recording rules increase TSDB load.
Mitigation: only add compatibility rules for metrics used by shipped dashboards/alerts; document a removal timeline.
